title: What Counts as Civilizational Reconfiguration?
summary: Not every change is a civilizational reconfiguration. The distinction depends on whether structures, relationships and functional carriers shift enough to alter how the system can continue, and on separating ordinary change from local failure and system-level reconfiguration.
shortAnswer: Not every change is a civilizational reconfiguration. The distinction depends on whether structures, relationships and functional carriers shift enough to alter how the system can continue, and on separating ordinary change from local failure and system-level reconfiguration.

blocks.text: Not every change is a civilizational reconfiguration. The distinction depends on whether structures, relationships and functional carriers shift enough to alter how the system can continue, and on separating ordinary change from local failure and system-level reconfiguration.

The threshold tightens across the three sections. Change may be absorbed by an existing arrangement; reconfiguration redistributes interfaces and functions; breakdown means the old arrangement can no longer maintain enough of its prior operation. These conditions can follow one another without being equivalent.

This article uses only definitions and structural relations in the completed Book VI manuscript. Conceptual boundaries are not presented as additional historical facts, and no new causal claims are added beyond the manuscript.
